solution:
Three equations \(a_ix + b_iy + c_i = 0\) are consistent if \(\begin{vmatrix} a_1 & b_1 & c_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 & c_2 \\ a_3 & b_3 & c_3 \end{vmatrix} = 0\).

\(\begin{vmatrix} 2 & -1 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & -2 \\ 11 & 2 & -3 \end{vmatrix} = 2(-3+4) + 1(-9+22) + 3(6-11) = 2 + 13 - 15 = 0\)

Since the determinant is \(0\), the equations are consistent.

\(\therefore\) the equations are consistent.

Write every equation in the form \(ax + by + c = 0\): \(2x + 3y - 4 = 0,\; x + 2y - 3 = 0,\; 3x + 4y + 5 = 0\).

The equations are consistent only if \(\begin{vmatrix} a_1 & b_1 & c_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 & c_2 \\ a_3 & b_3 & c_3 \end{vmatrix} = 0\).

\(\begin{vmatrix} 2 & 3 & -4 \\ 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 3 & 4 & 5 \end{vmatrix} = 2(10+12) - 3(5+9) - 4(4-6) = 44 - 42 + 8 = 10\)

Since the determinant is \(10 \ne 0\), the equations are not consistent.

\(\therefore\) the equations are not consistent.
_note: Stem as printed: the middle equation is given as \(x + 2y = 3\) while its neighbours are in \(\dots = 0\) form. Solved exactly as printed (i.e. \(x + 2y - 3 = 0\)); the solution opens by putting all three into the common form so the determinant test is well defined. Answer agrees with the book (Not Consistent).

\(\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 7 & 4 & -11 \\ 2 & 4 & -6 \end{vmatrix} = 1(-24+44) - 2(-42+22) - 3(28-8) = 20 + 40 - 60 = 0\)

(Indeed \(R_3 = 2R_1\), so the determinant vanishes.)

Since the determinant is \(0\), the equations are consistent.

\(\therefore\) the equations are consistent.

The equations are consistent, so \(\begin{vmatrix} 2 & 3 & -2 \\ 2 & 4 & -k \\ 1 & -2 & 3k \end{vmatrix} = 0\).

Expanding along the first row:

\(2(12k - 2k) - 3(6k + k) - 2(-4 - 4) = 0\)

\(20k - 21k + 16 = 0\)

\(-k + 16 = 0\)

\(\therefore k = 16\)

Writing \(x + y = 0\) as \(x + y + 0 = 0\), consistency requires \(\begin{vmatrix} k & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = 0\).

Expanding along the first row:

\(k(0 - 1) - 3(0 - 1) + 1(1 - 2) = 0\)

\(-k + 3 - 1 = 0\)

\(-k + 2 = 0\)

\(\therefore k = 2\)

Area \(= \dfrac{1}{2}\left| \begin{vmatrix} x_1 & y_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & 1 \\ x_3 & y_3 & 1 \end{vmatrix} \right|\) with A\((5, 8)\), B\((5, 0)\), C\((1, 0)\):

\(\begin{vmatrix} 5 & 8 & 1 \\ 5 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 5(0-0) - 8(5-1) + 1(0-0) = -32\)

Area \(= \dfrac{1}{2}\left|-32\right| = 16\)

\(\therefore\) the area of the triangle is \(16\) sq. unit.

With P\(\left(\dfrac{3}{2}, 1\right)\), Q\((4, 2)\), R\(\left(4, -\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\):

\(\begin{vmatrix} \dfrac{3}{2} & 1 & 1 \\ 4 & 2 & 1 \\ 4 & -\dfrac{1}{2} & 1 \end{vmatrix} = \dfrac{3}{2}\left(2 + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) - 1(4 - 4) + 1(-2 - 8) = \dfrac{3}{2}\cdot\dfrac{5}{2} - 0 - 10 = \dfrac{15}{4} - 10 = -\dfrac{25}{4}\)

Area \(= \dfrac{1}{2}\left|-\dfrac{25}{4}\right| = \dfrac{25}{8}\)

\(\therefore\) the area of the triangle is \(\dfrac{25}{8}\) sq. unit.

Join the diagonal AC, so that quadrilateral ABCD splits into \(\triangle\)ABC and \(\triangle\)ACD.

For \(\triangle\)ABC with A\((-3, 1)\), B\((-2, -2)\), C\((3, -1)\):

\(\begin{vmatrix} -3 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & -2 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = -3(-2+1) - 1(-2-3) + 1(2+6) = 3 + 5 + 8 = 16\), so area \(= \dfrac{1}{2}(16) = 8\).

For \(\triangle\)ACD with A\((-3, 1)\), C\((3, -1)\), D\((1, 4)\):

\(\begin{vmatrix} -3 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 4 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = -3(-1-4) - 1(3-1) + 1(12+1) = 15 - 2 + 13 = 26\), so area \(= \dfrac{1}{2}(26) = 13\).

Area of quadrilateral ABCD \(= 8 + 13 = 21\)

\(\therefore\) the area of the quadrilateral is \(21\) sq. unit.

The points are collinear if \(\begin{vmatrix} x_1 & y_1 & 1 \\ x_2 & y_2 & 1 \\ x_3 & y_3 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 0\).

With A\((3, -1)\), B\((0, -3)\), C\((12, 5)\):

\(\begin{vmatrix} 3 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 12 & 5 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 3(-3-5) + 1(0-12) + 1(0+36) = -24 - 12 + 36 = 0\)

The determinant is \(0\), so the triangle ABC has zero area.

\(\therefore\) the points A, B, C are collinear.

With P\((3, -5)\), Q\((6, 1)\), R\((4, 2)\):

\(\begin{vmatrix} 3 & -5 & 1 \\ 6 & 1 & 1 \\ 4 & 2 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 3(1-2) + 5(6-4) + 1(12-4) = -3 + 10 + 8 = 15\)

The determinant is \(15 \ne 0\), so the three points form a triangle of area \(\dfrac{15}{2}\) sq. unit.

\(\therefore\) the points P, Q, R are not collinear.

With L\(\left(0, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\), M\((2, -1)\), N\(\left(-4, \dfrac{7}{2}\right)\):

\(\begin{vmatrix} 0 & \dfrac{1}{2} & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 \\ -4 & \dfrac{7}{2} & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 0\left(-1 - \dfrac{7}{2}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}(2 + 4) + 1(7 - 4) = 0 - 3 + 3 = 0\)

The determinant is \(0\), so the triangle LMN has zero area.

\(\therefore\) the points L, M, N are collinear.
